# Incident — Style Reference

> Linen-stock incident logbook with a single flame struck in the margin. A weight-400 book serif sets every headline over #ffffff and #f8f5f0 paper, hairlines run at 8% ink, and #f25533 is the only lit match.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Incident speaks a warm-broadsheet product language: an on-call platform that sets its emergencies in a book serif instead of a siren palette. The canvas is Paper #ffffff (43 uses), layered with Linen Surface #f8f5f0 (28) and Sand Parchment #f1ebe2 (22) for section bands, secondary pills and diagram rails, while Ink #161618 (80 uses) carries text. The chromatic budget is exactly one hue, Ember Signal #f25533, permitted on the primary pill CTA, the logo flame, diagram glyphs and the closing footer band. Every other saturated value lives inside product mockups. STKBureauSerif at weight 400 owns all headlines from 36px to 80px, with tracking tightened to -0.04em at display size. The 1.82 jump from heading to display dwarfs a conventional Major Third. STKBureauSans at 400–500 handles UI with -0.01em tracking. Shapes split cleanly between 9999px pills for actions and 12px cards, and elevation is a whisper of 2–16% ink shadow. The site reads as a calm editorial post-mortem rather than an alarm dashboard.

## Tokens — Colors

It is the single saturated hue in the chrome, so it marks every place the page wants a decision. Do not dilute it into body links or section backgrounds. |

| Carbon Panel | `#1c1c1f` | `--color-carbon-panel` | Dark action buttons inside the incident-alert mockup and the inverted alert card. It is the only dark surface, and it is quoted from the product rather than used as page chrome. |

| Pewter Meta | `#6d6d70` | `--color-pewter-meta` | Timestamps, "Grafana · Just now" metadata and job titles beside names (16 uses). It is the tertiary step, used for facts nobody needs to read first. |
| Ink Hairline | `#16161814` | `--color-ink-hairline` | Story dividers, nav dropdown rules and card edges (15 uses). Ink at 8% alpha tints correctly on both Paper and Linen, so the border adapts to the surface beneath it. |
| Quartz Border | `#e8e8ea` | `--color-quartz-border` | Prompt-chip outlines and mockup panel edges (8 uses). It is the cool, opaque border for product UI only, the counterpart to the warm hairline. |

## Tokens — Typography

### STKBureauSerif — the display voice, a weight-400 book serif reserved for headlines · `--font-stk-bureau-serif`

- **Substitute:** Newsreader Display at 400, Source Serif 4 (display optical size) at 400, Fraunces at 350 with SOFT 0 and WONK 0. Bureau Serif draws slightly lighter than its nominal 400, with fine hairlines and moderate contrast. Match that thin stroke and avoid any substitute that renders as a 500.
- **Weights:** 400
- **Sizes:** 36px, 44px, 80px
- **Line height:** 1.0, 1.1, 1.15
- **Letter spacing:** -0.9px at 36px, -1.32px at 44px, -3.2px at 80px
- **Role:** Weight 400 at 80px is the signature. Headlines are enormous and quiet, which is the opposite of the 700-weight sans most SaaS heroes use. Tracking tightens progressively from -0.025em to -0.04em as size grows, so the letters knit into a single inked line. The scale moves 36 → 44 → 80. The first step is a Minor Third (1.22), and the second leaps 1.82, a deliberate two-tier system of section headline and statement headline with nothing in between.

### STKBureauSans — the UI and body voice, a neutral grotesk carrying all functional text · `--font-stk-bureau-sans`

- **Substitute:** Inter at 400 and 500, Geist at 400 and 500, Hanken Grotesk at 450 and 550. Bureau Sans draws true to its nominal weight with slightly narrow proportions. Inter matches stroke weight one-for-one, and Hanken needs the half-step up to avoid reading thin.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600, 700
- **Sizes:** 12px, 13px, 16px, 17px, 18px, 24px
- **Line height:** 1.333, 1.4, 1.3
- **Letter spacing:** 0px at 12px, -0.13px at 13px, -0.16px at 16px, -0.17px at 17px, -0.18px at 18px, -0.24px at 24px
- **Role:** This is the workhorse, with 101 uses at 400 and 82 at 500. Weight 500 is the action weight on buttons, nav and labels, and 600 or 700 appear only inside mockups. Tracking is a uniform -0.01em above 12px, a systematic tightening that keeps the grotesk from feeling looser than the serif beside it. Pairing a grotesk with a book serif is the editorial convention. Applying it to an incident-response product is the anti-convention move.

### Geist Mono — the technical voice inside product mockups · `--font-geist-mono`

- **Substitute:** Geist Mono at 400 (freely available), JetBrains Mono at 400, IBM Plex Mono at 400. Geist Mono draws light and even, so avoid Plex at 500.
- **Weights:** 400, 600
- **Sizes:** 11px, 14px
- **Line height:** 1.375, 1.46
- **Letter spacing:** 0px at 11px, 0px at 14px
- **Role:** It appears 45 times, all inside quoted product UI: service names, error payloads and IDs. It signals "this is real system output" and keeps engineering texture out of the marketing type. Inter (8–10px) and Lato (10–12px) also render inside Slack-style mockups. They are mockup-internal faces, not system families.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | STKBureauSans | 400 | 12px | 1.333 | 0px | `--text-small` |
| caption | STKBureauSans | 400 | 13px | 1.4 | -0.13px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Geist Mono | 400 | 14px | 1.375 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | STKBureauSans | 400 | 16px | 1.4 | -0.16px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | STKBureauSans | 500 | 18px | 1.4 | -0.18px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | STKBureauSans | 400 | 24px | 1.3 | -0.24px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | STKBureauSerif | 400 | 36px | 1.15 | -0.9px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | STKBureauSerif | 400 | 44px | 1.1 | -1.32px | `--text-heading` |
| display | STKBureauSerif | 400 | 80px | 1.0 | -3.2px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline in STKBureauSerif at weight 400: 36px, 44px or 80px with -0.9px, -1.32px or -3.2px tracking. Size alone carries hierarchy, which is the whole thesis.
- Spend #f25533 on four things only: the primary pill, the logo flame, diagram glyphs and the footer band. One hue keeps the urgency color meaningful on a product about urgency.
- Use a 9999px radius for every action and chip, and 12px for content cards. The two-shape vocabulary lets a reader tell clickable from readable at a glance.
- Alternate #ffffff and #f8f5f0 section bands with 96px vertical rhythm. Tonal shifts do the separating work that borders and shadows do elsewhere.
- Draw dividers as 1px #16161814 rather than an opaque gray. The 8% ink tint stays correct on both Paper and Linen.
- Set UI and buttons in STKBureauSans 500 at 16px or 18px with -0.01em tracking. A medium grotesk gives actions enough density to stand beside the light serif.
- Place a 24px #656567 subheading directly under 80px display type with 24px between them. The 3.33 size ratio frames the serif as a statement and the sans as an explanation.

### Don't

- Don't bold the serif to 600 or 700 for emphasis. Heavy serifs turn the calm post-mortem voice into a tabloid banner and break the weight-400 thesis.
- Don't introduce a second brand hue, such as a blue secondary button or a red alert banner. The secondary is #f8f5f0, and extra hues demote #f25533 from signal to decoration.
- Don't square buttons off to the 8px card radius. Actions are 9999px pills, and an 8px button blurs the line between control and content.
- Don't set body copy in #000000. Jet Ink is reserved for serif headlines, and body runs at #161618 or #656567 so long text stays softer than display type.
- Don't stack shadows deeper than the 0.16-alpha `xl` value. Anything heavier makes the paper canvas look like a floating dashboard.
- Don't use cool #f3f3f4 or #f7f7f8 for marketing section bands. Cool grays belong to quoted product UI, and mixing them into the chrome erases the warm-cool boundary.
- Don't swap the 80px display serif for a sans to "feel more technical". A grotesk hero is what every competitor ships, and the serif must never be traded away.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #ffffff (Paper)
- secondary surface: #f8f5f0 (Linen Surface)
- deeper warm surface: #f1ebe2 (Sand Parchment)
- headline text: #000000 (Jet Ink)
- body text: #161618 (Ink)
- secondary text: #656567 (Slate Caption)
- hairline: #16161814 (Ink Hairline)
- primary action: #f25533 (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts use #f25533 as a solid fill for exactly one highlighted series. Every other series renders in #f1ebe2, #6d6d70 or #f25533 at 16% opacity, so the accent marks the single number that matters and never floods the visualisation.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button: an anchor with a background of #f25533, text color #f7f7f8, no border and border-radius 9999px. Use padding 12px 20px for a 49px height. The label is "Get a demo" in STKBureauSans (fallback Inter) at 18px, weight 500, line-height 1.4 and letter-spacing -0.18px, with no box-shadow. Place a secondary button 8px to its right with background #f8f5f0, text #161618 and an identical radius, padding and type. On hover, darken neither fill by more than one step and keep the shadow at none.

2. Build a hero section: a #ffffff full-width band with content centered inside a 1192px container and 96px top padding. The h1 is "With great product, comes great reliability" in STKBureauSerif (fallback Newsreader Display) at 80px, weight 400, line-height 1.0, letter-spacing -3.2px, color #000000 and max-width 794px. Add 24px below it, then a subtitle in STKBureauSans at 24px, weight 400, line-height 1.3, letter-spacing -0.24px and color #656567. Add 32px below that, then the Ember and Linen pill pair from prompt 1. Then add 96px of space and a 9-column, 2-row grid of black monochrome logos with a 48px row gap.

3. Build a customer story card: a two-column grid inside 1192px with a 64px column gap. The left column holds a co-brand logo row, then a STKBureauSerif headline at 36px, weight 400, line-height 1.15, letter-spacing -0.9px and color #161618. Below that comes a 16px STKBureauSans body in #656567, then a 16px quote in #161618. Next is a name at weight 500 in #161618 with a title in #6d6d70, then a 1px #16161814 divider with 24px above and below, and a "Read their story →" link at 16px weight 500 in #161618. The right column is a #f8f5f0 tile with a 12px radius, a 1:1 aspect ratio and no shadow. Center a #ffffff 9999px pill in it with 8px 16px padding and the shadow `0 1px 2px 0 rgba(10, 20, 33, 0.03), 0 2px 6px 0 rgba(10, 20, 33, 0.05)`.

4. Build a navigation bar: a sticky #ffffff header 80px tall, with content capped at 1192px. Place the wordmark on the left at a 32px height. In the center, add links "Products, Solutions, Resources, Customers, Pricing, Careers" in STKBureauSans at 16px, weight 500, line-height 1.0 and color #161618, each with 8px 12px padding. On the right, add a #f25533 "Get a demo" pill and a #f8f5f0 "Login" pill, both with a 9999px radius, 8px 16px padding, 16px weight 500 text and an 8px gap. Above the bar, add a #f8f5f0 announcement ribbon with an 8px radius and 8px padding, using a 16px weight 500 #656567 label followed by #161618 text.

### Pill Button — Ember (Primary)

**Role:** The single demo-request call to action

A lit match on paper. The spec is a #f25533 fill with #f7f7f8 text, no border, a 9999px radius, 12px 20px padding and a 49px height, set in STKBureauSans 18px at 500 with -0.18px tracking and no shadow. The nav instance compresses to 8px 16px padding, 38px height and 16px type. As the only orange element in the hero, it carries the system's entire chromatic budget for that viewport.

### Pill Button — Linen (Secondary)

**Role:** Low-commitment alternative beside the primary

A warm, recessive twin. The spec is a #f8f5f0 fill with #161618 text, no border, a 9999px radius, 12px 20px padding and a 49px height, set in STKBureauSans 18px at 500 with -0.18px tracking and no shadow. The nav "Login" uses 8px 16px padding at 16px. It deliberately skips the conventional outlined ghost button, since a tonal Linen fill stays visibly clickable without adding a line.

### Sticky Navigation Bar

**Role:** Persistent wayfinding with two pill actions

A filled, sticky 80px band capped at 1192px. The wordmark sits left at 130px wide, and six centered links sit in STKBureauSans 16px at 500 with 1.0 line height and 8px 12px padding. They measure #111827, a framework gray that is not a system token, so normalize them to #161618. The Ember and Linen pills sit right with an 8px gap on a #ffffff fill. It reads as a document header rather than an app toolbar.

### Announcement Bar

**Role:** Top-of-page event or content promotion

A soft, linen ribbon. The spec is a #f8f5f0 fill across the 1192px container with an 8px radius, 8px padding and centered STKBureauSans 16px at 500 with -0.16px tracking. The "Register:" prefix is #656567, the headline is #161618, and there is no border or shadow. It is the only content above the nav and is meant to whisper rather than flash.

### Customer Story Card

**Role:** Main proof unit, quote plus video

The main content card is a two-column editorial spread. On the left, a co-brand lockup sits over a STKBureauSerif 36px at 400 headline in #161618 with -0.9px tracking. Below it come a 16px #656567 body, a 16px #161618 quote, and a name in 500 with a #6d6d70 title. A 1px #16161814 divider and a "Read their story →" text link at 16px/500 close the column. On the right, a #f8f5f0 video tile uses a 12px radius with no shadow. The spread is a magazine feature, not a testimonial carousel.

### Watch Video Pill

**Role:** Play affordance on media tiles

A floating white capsule. The spec is a #ffffff fill with a 9999px radius, 8px 16px padding, a play glyph in #000000, "Watch video" in STKBureauSans 16px at 500 #161618 and a "3:47" duration in #6d6d70. It is centered in the Linen tile with the `sm` shadow. This is the only place a white element sits on Linen, and it inverts the usual surface order so the control reads as lifted.

### Segmented Toggle — Problem / Solution

**Role:** Binary narrative switch inside sections

A sand track with a paper thumb. The spec is a #f1ebe2 track with a 9999px radius and 4px padding, and an active segment of #ffffff at 9999px radius with 6px 12px padding. Labels use STKBureauSans 13px at 500 in #161618 with -0.13px tracking, and the thumb carries the `sm` shadow. It is a tab control drawn entirely in warm tones, so a story switch stays inside the editorial palette.

### Logo Wall

**Role:** Customer credibility, monochrome

A grayscale roll call. Nine columns by two rows sit across roughly 800px of the 1192px container, using monochrome #000000 logos at equal optical height (roughly 24px) with a 48px row gap. There are no cards, borders or color. A 1px #16161814 rule below separates it from the story. Logos are flattened to ink so that no customer brand color competes with #f25533.

### Product Mockup Tile

**Role:** Quoted product UI fragments

Cool, miniaturized product glass. The spec is a #f7f7f8 fill with an 8px radius, 0 12px padding and the `subtle` shadow. Inner text uses Inter 8–10px in #161618 and Geist Mono 11–14px. Inside the alert mockup, action buttons are #1c1c1f with #ffffff STKBureauSans 13px/500, a 7px radius and a 28px height. Their sibling #2a2a2e is mockup-internal. The 7px radius is a deliberate outlier: it quotes the real app's button shape, not the marketing system.

### Prompt Chip

**Role:** Suggested AI questions in mockups

A tiny cool capsule. The spec is a #f3f3f4 fill with a 1px #e8e8ea border, a 9999px radius and 4px 6px padding, with Inter 8px at 400 in #161618 and 1.0 line height. Chips appear in rows of three under AI-assistant mockups. They borrow the pill vocabulary at the smallest scale, so even quoted UI echoes the marketing CTA shape.

### Status Pill — Operational (Outlier)

**Role:** Root node of the response tree

A saturated green capsule and the system outlier. It uses an estimated deep green fill (decorative, not a system token) with #ffffff STKBureauSans 13px/500 text, a check glyph, a 9999px radius and 6px 12px padding. It roots a #f1ebe2 connector tree on a Linen band. Green is permitted only here because it depicts real status-page semantics, which makes it a product quotation rather than a palette expansion.

### Platform Arch Diagram

**Role:** Signature product-architecture illustration

Concentric arches as an org chart. The outer band fades from #f1ebe2 to #ffffff, and #16161814 radial dividers split it. A middle arch uses a pale orange tint (decorative, not a system token), and the core is a solid #f25533 dome with a #ffffff glyph. Product nodes are #ffffff 40px tiles with an 8px radius and an orange glyph, labeled in STKBureauSans 13px/500. Here the accent is finally allowed to fill area, in the single diagram that explains the whole product.

### Nav Dropdown — Brand Assets

**Role:** Contextual menu off the logo

A compact paper sheet. The spec is a #ffffff panel with an 8px radius, a `lg` shadow and a 12px 13px/500 "Brand Assets" header in #161618 over a #16161814 rule. Rows are 240px by 34px with 8px padding and a 4px radius, set in STKBureauSans 13px/400 with -0.13px tracking in #656567, each with a small orange file icon and a chevron. It is the densest component on the site and stays fully monochrome apart from the icons.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline in STKBureauSerif at weight 400: 36px, 44px or 80px with -0.9px, -1.32px or -3.2px tracking. Size alone carries hierarchy, which is the whole thesis.
- Spend #f25533 on four things only: the primary pill, the logo flame, diagram glyphs and the footer band. One hue keeps the urgency color meaningful on a product about urgency.
- Use a 9999px radius for every action and chip, and 12px for content cards. The two-shape vocabulary lets a reader tell clickable from readable at a glance.
- Alternate #ffffff and #f8f5f0 section bands with 96px vertical rhythm. Tonal shifts do the separating work that borders and shadows do elsewhere.
- Draw dividers as 1px #16161814 rather than an opaque gray. The 8% ink tint stays correct on both Paper and Linen.
- Set UI and buttons in STKBureauSans 500 at 16px or 18px with -0.01em tracking. A medium grotesk gives actions enough density to stand beside the light serif.
- Place a 24px #656567 subheading directly under 80px display type with 24px between them. The 3.33 size ratio frames the serif as a statement and the sans as an explanation.

### Don't

- Don't bold the serif to 600 or 700 for emphasis. Heavy serifs turn the calm post-mortem voice into a tabloid banner and break the weight-400 thesis.
- Don't introduce a second brand hue, such as a blue secondary button or a red alert banner. The secondary is #f8f5f0, and extra hues demote #f25533 from signal to decoration.
- Don't square buttons off to the 8px card radius. Actions are 9999px pills, and an 8px button blurs the line between control and content.
- Don't set body copy in #000000. Jet Ink is reserved for serif headlines, and body runs at #161618 or #656567 so long text stays softer than display type.
- Don't stack shadows deeper than the 0.16-alpha `xl` value. Anything heavier makes the paper canvas look like a floating dashboard.
- Don't use cool #f3f3f4 or #f7f7f8 for marketing section bands. Cool grays belong to quoted product UI, and mixing them into the chrome erases the warm-cool boundary.
- Don't swap the 80px display serif for a sans to "feel more technical". A grotesk hero is what every competitor ships, and the serif must never be traded away.

## Imagery

There is no photography beyond 22px circular avatars in mockups. The imagery is product UI quoted as artifacts: Slack-style threads in Lato, incident cards in Inter, and alert panels with #1c1c1f buttons. All of it is framed in 8px or 12px rounded containers on #f7f7f8 or #f8f5f0, with the `subtle` to `xl` shadows and no borders. Window chrome dots appear as decorative-only colors that are not system tokens (#ff5f57, #febc2e, #28c840). Icons are small, filled orange glyphs inside 40px white 8px-radius tiles. Customer logos are flattened to black. The only gradient is the arch band fading from #f1ebe2 to #ffffff, which is decorative rather than a system token, with no glows or orbs. The narrative is that the product is the illustration, and the brand never needs a stock photo to explain an outage.

## Layout

Content is capped at 1192px, with wider bands reaching 1512px, inside a 1920px page, and sections are separated by 96px to 160px. The hero is centered: an 80px serif headline at 794px width, a 24px #656567 subtitle and two pills with an 8px gap, followed by a 9-by-2 monochrome logo wall. Sections alternate Paper and Linen. A two-column customer story uses 588px halves, a Linen "Problem / Solution" band holds a status tree, and a white "Meet the platform" band holds the arch diagram. The four feature h3s sit in 400px columns. The nav is sticky, filled and 80px tall, with the logo left, links centered and pills right, and an announcement ribbon above it. The footer is a full-bleed #f25533 band with #ffffff text, 160px top and 56px bottom padding. At 375px, drop the display to the 44px heading size and use 64px section gaps. The overall density is comfortable.

## Serif Restraint

The discipline is that hierarchy is bought with size and tracking, not weight. Every serif glyph on the page is 400, from the 36px story headline to the 80px statement, and tracking scales from -0.025em to -0.04em to hold the light strokes together. This is a calm, broadsheet voice for a product category that conventionally shouts in bold sans and red. It breaks the moment someone sets a 700 serif, adds italics for emphasis, or invents an in-between 56px size that blurs the two-tier system. To extend it, add new headline contexts only at 36px, 44px or 80px. Push emphasis into the sans at 500, or into Ember color on a single word, rather than into the serif's weight.

## One-Flame Budget

The chromatic budget is exactly one hue, and that rule is non-negotiable. #f25533 appears on the primary pill, the logo flame, the 40px diagram glyphs, the arch core and the footer band. Everything else is warm neutral (#ffffff, #f8f5f0, #f1ebe2) or ink. Saturated greens, blues and reds exist only inside quoted product mockups, where they depict real Slack, status-page or avatar colors. The system breaks when a feature section gets a blue accent, a link turns orange, or a "new" badge borrows Ember at small size and dilutes the CTA. To extend it, give any new emphasis a Linen or Sand surface first. If color is still required, use #f25533 at area scale once per viewport and nowhere else.

## Warm-Cool Separation

The chrome is warm and the product is cool, and that split is how the page tells marketing from evidence. Marketing surfaces use #f8f5f0 and #f1ebe2 with STKBureau type and 8%-ink hairlines. Quoted UI uses #f7f7f8, #f3f3f4 and #e8e8ea with Inter, Lato and Geist Mono at 8–14px. The boundary breaks if a section band is filled with #f3f3f4, or if a mockup card adopts Linen. Either change makes screenshots look like decoration rather than proof. To extend it, render any new product fragment in the cool trio with an 8px radius and the `subtle` shadow, and keep every new marketing container on the warm pair with a 12px radius and no shadow.

## Similar Brands

- **Incident** — Shares Anthropic's weight-400 book serif over warm cream with a single clay-orange accent, though Incident pushes the orange to full-bleed area in its footer band.
- **Incident** — Shares Mercury's large, light serif headlines on a fintech-grade product page, but Mercury rations color even further and leans on photography Incident does not use.
- **Incident** — Is a category competitor to PagerDuty, which stakes the same on-call territory with a bold sans and a saturated green. Incident's serif is a deliberate inversion of that convention.
- **Incident** — Is a category competitor to Rootly, which shares the product-mockup-as-illustration approach, while Rootly keeps a conventional sans hero and a cooler, purple-led palette.
